case_name: Lajo Devi vs Union Of India And Others.
facts_of_case: Sh. Kheru Ram was married to Melo Devi. He died in harness while serving in MES. Lajo Devi claimed to be his second wife. She received family pension till she expired on 16th January, 2000.

legal_principles.principle: Any marriage solemnized during subsistence of first marriage and during the lifetime of the first wife is null and void.
legal_principles.held: After coming into force of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, any marriage solemnized after commencement of this enactment during subsistence of the first marriage and during life time of the first wife was null and void in terms of Section 11 thereof.

legal_principles.principle: Rule 54(7)(a)(i) and (ii) of the CCS(Pension) Rules, 1972 applies only where polygamy marriages were recognized in law.
legal_principles.held: So far as the applicability of Rule 54(7)(a)(i) and (ii) of the CCS(Pension) Rules, 1972 is concerned, the learned Single Judge has, in our view, again rightly observed that the same would apply only where polygamy marriages were recognized in law.

outcome.final_order: The delay of 9 days in filing the appeal is condoned.

keywords: Latin maxim: Nemo judex in causa sua
use_for_drafting: condoning delay in filing an appeal
